name: Coronet Blue
summary: Edgerunners wake in a dangerous spot with no memory of who they are while everyone else treats them as known.

name: Crisis
summary: Edgerunners are dropped into a citywide or worldwide disaster that must tie directly to the game's plot.

name: Discovery
summary: The adventure opens with a find, such as lost pre-War tech or a dangerous datafile, linked to a later element.

name: False Accusation
summary: Edgerunners are blamed for a crime they did not commit and are left with only fight or flee.

name: Kidnapped
summary: Edgerunners, or a friend of theirs, are taken by a mysterious and far stronger force.

name: Looming Threat
summary: Like Crisis, but the danger has not yet broken; portents and massing forces signal that it is coming.

name: Murder
summary: The game opens with a killing the Edgerunners cannot solve by capturing the murderer, linking it to the plot.

name: Play a Cliffhanger
summary: Open with an action scene (Confrontation, Ambush or Fist Fight work best) that introduces opposition or allies.

name: Play a Development
summary: Open with a Development (Secret Meeting, Mistaken Identity, Romance or Treachery) that introduces major allies or foes.

name: Revelation
summary: A hidden fact, such as a secret past or an inheritance, changes the Edgerunners' lives and links to the game.

name: Ambush
summary: A fight where one side gets a free first shot; when run against the Edgerunners they check Awareness against the foe's Stealth.

name: Battle
summary: A formal open combat free-for-all; scale successive battles from Mooks to Lieutenants to Mini Bosses (1 Mook = 1, 1 Lieutenant = 2, 1 Mini Boss = 3 Edgerunners).

name: Chase
summary: The Crew pursues the opposition; works best right after a Kidnapping or Revelation.

name: Confrontation
summary: A verbal, non-physical showdown of threats and intimidation where the stronger side chooses not to attack.

name: Contest
summary: A ritualized one-on-one competition, such as riddles or feats; the GM may not simply decree the NPC wins.

name: Dogfight
summary: Vehicular combat in air, on roads or on water, where the opposition tries to shoot the Edgerunners down.

name: Duel
summary: One-on-one combat between evenly matched participants, not necessarily to the death.

name: Fist Fight
summary: Hand-to-hand, weaponless combat between the Edgerunners (or a champion) and the opposition, often ritualized.

name: Monster
summary: A non-intelligent threat such as a guard drone, automated turrets or a drone horde.

name: Obstacles
summary: Traps and hazards, lethal or non-lethal, that must be physically overcome and must always be beatable with clues present.

name: Pursuit
summary: The Edgerunners are chased by a clearly superior force and must run.

name: Race
summary: The Edgerunners race the opposition to a person, place or thing; best after a Revelation or Discovery.

name: Skirmish!
summary: A small battle where a winning Crew sees the foe escape and a losing Crew is captured or left wounded.

name: Advantage Revealed
summary: The Edgerunners uncover a previously unknown ability, tool or weapon.

name: Alliance
summary: Outside help arrives, giving the Edgerunners a new manpower resource that must not decide the outcome alone.

name: Back from the Dead
summary: An old opponent returns from a supposed death; use once, with a plausible escape.

name: Betrayal
summary: A trusted ally, lover or contact betrays the Party; the Edgerunners must get a chance to catch or avenge it.

name: Clue
summary: An ambiguous Revelation that reveals only one part of the puzzle.

name: Foreshadowing
summary: An ambiguous hint of coming events, played well before the event.

name: Framed!
summary: The Party or a member is set up for a crime they did not commit, obviously to everyone but the authorities.

name: Gain Mastery
summary: A compressed period of training or learning that gives the Edgerunners the skills they need.

name: Hazardous Quest
summary: A long arduous journey with environmental dangers and only minor unrelated combat.

name: Hesitation
summary: The opposition breaks off an attack to negotiate a temporary truce, then usually betrays it.

name: Lie Revealed
summary: Something believed true is shown to be a lie, without revealing the truth.

name: Mistaken Identity
summary: An Edgerunner is mistaken for, or poses as, an important someone else, bringing problems or advantages.

name: Monologue
summary: The opposition leader brags about the plan when the Edgerunners are fully in their control.

name: Not What it Seems
summary: An earlier action turns out to differ from how it was first perceived, such as a double agent.

name: Obsession
summary: Another character becomes obsessed with a Party member and follows them without attacking.

name: Personal Stake
summary: The stakes are raised by something personal, such as a poisoning, a kidnapped loved one or a frame-up.

name: Puzzle
summary: A riddle or puzzle with one side only that must be solved to proceed and must always have clues to a solution.

name: Rescuers!
summary: The Edgerunners must rescue someone from capture, death or confinement, with a compelling reason to do so.

name: Retreat
summary: Usually after a Cliffhanger, the opponents break off an action and withdraw to a stronghold, covering their tracks with a delaying tactic.

name: Revealed Weakness
summary: The Edgerunners learn a clearly described weakness of the opposition: physical, mental, a special tool or a traitor.

name: Revelation
summary: The whole story is revealed in one shot; use only when knowing it will not critically affect the outcome.

name: Romance
summary: Romance comes to one or more of the Edgerunners.

name: Sabotage!
summary: A Party weapon, cyberware or vehicle is disabled; like Betrayal, the Party gets a chance to detect or repair it.

name: Second Chance
summary: Another crack at a problem the Edgerunners failed, which the GM must justify.

name: Secret Meeting
summary: A clandestine meeting to gain allies or information, usually played before a Clue, Revelation or Alliance.

name: Strange Bedfellows
summary: A common threat forces the Crew and the opposition to work together.

name: Turnabout!
summary: A member of the opposition decides to aid the Crew, for example an underling who betrays the Antagonist.

name: Vengeance!
summary: One Crew member becomes the opposition's target for vengeance and is repeatedly singled out.

name: Warning
summary: An explicit notice of a coming threat, in contrast to the vague hints of Foreshadowing.

name: Final Battle
summary: The last showdown with the Antagonist, henchmen and monsters, a dramatic free-for-all that wraps up the game.

name: Final Revelation
summary: The gathered cast must work out and expose the underlying mystery; the outcome is already decided.

name: Final Act
summary: The Edgerunners carry out their big plan, as in a heist, with the focus on how the plan pieces fit together rather than combat.

name: Antagonist Escapes
summary: The Antagonist is beaten but gets clean away, available for reuse.

name: Antagonist is Killed
summary: The Antagonist dies and the GM awards I.P.

name: Antagonist Toppled
summary: The Antagonist survives but the threat is neutralized, for example by prison, disgrace or loss of followers.

name: Edgerunners Captured
summary: The Edgerunners are captured when the adventure ends; the GM may run a different game before the next.

name: Edgerunners Escape
summary: The Edgerunners are rescued or escape when on the ropes, saved for another round.

name: Ending Cliffhanger
summary: A new threat appears just as the Edgerunners celebrate, setting up a sequel.

name: Greater Threat
summary: A far greater threat stands behind the defeated Antagonist, showing that this is only the beginning.

name: Happy Ending
summary: The Edgerunners win the day, whether a major or minor victory.

name: Pyrrhic Victory
summary: The Edgerunners win technically but at a heavy cost.
